text: Sinead starts her new job at the library on Monday. Remind me to text her the evening before to say good luck.
Louis is a die-hard Leeds fan and has had a season ticket since he was twelve. He also plays bass in a covers band on Thursdays.
Caught up with Anika after work. Her dad is retiring at the end of March 2027 after thirty years on the buses, and the family are planning a surprise party for him.
Ellie said her brother Santiago got the promotion to shift manager. She's thrilled for him. I should send him a congratulations message this weekend.
Need to renew the car insurance before 2 November 2026.
Catalina knits constantly, mostly socks and baby blankets. She mentioned she'd love a proper wooden yarn bowl, which might be a good birthday idea.
Phoebe's leaving drinks are on Friday at the Crown. Don't forget to get a card and pass it round the office on Thursday so everyone can sign it.
Ming is really nervous about her first day as a junior doctor next Tuesday. Remind me to message her that morning, and then ring her the day after to see how it went.

Bogdan's retirement do has been called off because his wife is unwell. He sounded quite low about it all. He'd been looking forward to it since the summer, and his daughter Ilse had already booked the hall and a band. They might do something small at home in the spring instead, once his wife is back on her feet. I should pop round with some soup next week.
Marisol has been reading her way through every Agatha Christie in order. She's on number forty-one and swears she still can't guess the murderer.

Spoke to Aisha on the phone. Her husband Hamza starts at the engineering firm in a fortnight, and they're moving to Bristol the week after. She's excited but worried about finding a school for their kids, especially the youngest, who has only just settled where they are. Hamza's boss has said he can work from home for the first month, which helps. Remind me to send Aisha the list of schools my cousin recommended before Friday.
Wiremu plays touch rugby every Sunday and supports the Hurricanes. Ask him about the final next time I see him.
I'm taking Katarzyna to the airport on Saturday morning, so I can't do the market this week.
Samir finished his last shift at the restaurant yesterday. He's starting a pastry course in January 2027. Remind me to ask him how the first week goes.
Manon's cat Biscuit had an operation on his paw this morning. She's been anxious all day. I should check in with her tomorrow evening.
Naledi has just been made head of the science department. Her mum told me at church, and she is clearly very proud. Must send Naledi flowers before the end of the week.
Ilse collects vintage board games, especially anything from the seventies. She has three different editions of Cluedo and wants an original Mastermind.
Kemal and his partner Noor are celebrating ten years together on 14 December. They're going back to Istanbul for a week to mark it.
Remind me to ask Kiara how her interview with the council went. It was on Wednesday afternoon.
Zofia's daughter has her grade five piano exam next Thursday. Zofia says she's practising for hours every evening and barely sleeping.
Quick note: Eli has stopped playing chess online and taken up climbing instead. He goes to the wall on Mondays and Fridays with his flatmate.
Alana's grandad passed away last weekend. The funeral is on Thursday 29 October. I need to send her a card, and maybe offer to help with food the day before.
Hassan left the bank after eleven years and is going freelance. He sounded relieved more than anything. His first big client meeting is next Monday.

Had coffee with Claire and Lena. Claire is training for the Dublin marathon and Lena has joined a ceramics class on Tuesday nights. Lena says the wheel is much harder than it looks and she's made nothing but wonky bowls so far. Claire's race is on Sunday 25 October, and she's aiming for under four hours. Her knee has been playing up, though, and she's worried she'll have to pull out halfway.
Carmen's son Eli is starting his apprenticeship as an electrician on 9 November 2026. She's asked me to keep an eye out for second-hand work boots in his size.

Zoe is struggling at the new job. Her manager keeps moving deadlines and she's thinking of handing in her notice in the new year. Her boyfriend thinks she should leave now rather than wait, and she has been crying in the car before work. She has an informal chat with a recruiter on Thursday. I should take her out for lunch soon, and remind me to ask how the recruiter call went on Friday.
Book the boiler service for sometime in the week of 16 November.
Sinead mentioned that her husband is a huge Bowie fan and collects the original vinyl pressings. Good to know for Christmas.
Caroline said she's finally retiring in June 2027. She wants to spend the first summer walking the Camino with her sister Ellie.
Louis and Anika are hosting a games night next Saturday. I'm bringing the snacks and the new expansion for Wingspan.
Remind me to call Santiago the day after his performance review on Friday. He's convinced it's going to go badly.
Catalina, or Cat as everyone at the club calls her, has been picked for the county netball squad. Trials were last month and she found out on Tuesday. Must congratulate her properly at training.
Phoebe's mum is having her hip replacement on 3 December. Phoebe will be staying with her for a fortnight afterwards, so she'll be off work. I should check how they're both doing that weekend.
Ming got the job at the design studio! She starts in March 2027, once her notice period is up.

Bogdan supports Dinamo Bucharest and watches every match, even at three in the morning when they play abroad. He also restores old radios in his shed and has about forty of them, some from before the war. His granddaughter Zoe has started helping him on Saturdays, and he says she's better at soldering than he is. He'd love a proper valve tester if I ever see one going cheap.

Talked to Marisol for ages tonight. Her sister Carmen has just found out she's expecting, due in May. Marisol is going to be an aunt for the first time and keeps sending me pictures of tiny cardigans she wants to knit. She also told me she's applying for the deputy manager role at the garden centre, with interviews in the week of 23 November. I said I'd help her practise questions the weekend before.
Aisha's book club has picked a Russian novel for December and she's already regretting it. She prefers crime and anything set in Scotland.
Wiremu's first day as a ranger at the national park is tomorrow. Text him tomorrow evening to ask how it went.
Plan for this weekend: clean out the garage, take the old bike to the tip and finally sort the spare room.
Hamza's brother Samir is getting married on 12 June 2027 in Lahore. Hamza is the best man and is already panicking about the speech.
Katarzyna's dog Pepper has gone missing from the park near her flat. She's put posters up everywhere. Don't forget to share her post on the neighbourhood group tonight.
Mrs Moreau next door is leaving the school after twenty-two years of teaching. Her last day is Friday 18 December. Remind me to get a card signed by the street the week before.

Manon is obsessed with Formula One and has a Ferrari cap she never takes off. She's going to the Abu Dhabi race this year with her brother Samir, which has been the plan since they were teenagers. They fly out on Thursday 3 December and come back the following Tuesday. She has also started a fantasy league at work and is, by her own admission, terrible at it.
Naledi said the job offer from the hospital fell through, so the move to Cape Town is off for now. She's staying put and trying to stay positive.
Dr Haddad said my results should be back by next Wednesday. Ring the surgery on Thursday if I haven't heard.
Ilse is coeliac and doesn't drink, so bear that in mind for the dinner on 7 November. Her partner Kemal eats anything.
Noor has started her PhD in marine biology and is spending most of the term in Plymouth. She seems happy but a bit lonely.

Kiara's band are playing their first proper gig at the Lantern on 21 November 2026. She's the drummer and says she feels sick every time she thinks about it. Remind me to message her good luck that afternoon, and to book tickets for me and Zoe tomorrow.
Zofia was made redundant on Monday. It came out of nowhere. She has a meeting with HR next week to talk through the package. I need to check in with her after that.
Eli loves Studio Ghibli films and draws fan art of the characters. His favourite is Howl's Moving Castle. A framed print might be a nice present.
Picked up the dry cleaning. Still need to post the parcel to Mum before Friday.
Alana and her husband have a new rescue dog called Juno. They're taking her to puppy classes on Saturday mornings.
Hassan Ahmed from the five-a-side team has been offered a coaching job with the under-twelves. He hasn't decided yet but said he'll let me know by the end of next week.
Claire's first day at the law firm went well, apparently. She said the people are lovely but the coffee is terrible.
Uncle Louis turns seventy on Sunday 8 November. Auntie wants everyone to bring a photo from a different decade for the party. Remind me to dig out the one from the caravan holiday the night before.
Lena got into the community choir she auditioned for. Rehearsals start next Tuesday.

Spoke to Carmen briefly. Her daughter has the driving test on Thursday, which is the third attempt, and she's in bits about it. Carmen herself starts a new part-time role at the pharmacy on Monday. I should text the daughter good luck on Wednesday night and ask Carmen how the first shift went the next day.
Zoe sent me her new running playlist. Mostly nineties dance tracks. She's doing the Parkrun every Saturday now and trying to get under twenty-five minutes.

Caroline Lewis rang to say the leaving lunch for Sinead is moved from Thursday to Friday 13 November. Same restaurant, 12:30. Sinead still thinks it's just a quiet lunch with her team, but about twenty people are coming, including her old boss Mr Rossi. Don't forget to pay Caroline the twenty pounds for the gift before then.
Lovely evening. Nothing much to note, just good food and a long walk by the river.
